title: Concatenating a numeric string with a nonempty string is truthy in either order

ground_truth.statement: A numeric string has at least one byte. Concatenation with another nonempty string has length at least two, hence is neither the empty string nor the one-byte string '0', the only falsey strings in PHP. The non-falsy-string return contract is sound in both orders.

provenance.derivation: General parameter contracts replace asserted local variable types.

notes: A return contract exposes inference through diagnostics without using an analyzer's inferred type as the oracle. Shares criterion with the two-nonempty-string variant. PHPStan and Psalm accept both returns. Mago reports invalid-return-statement on lines 9 and 17 because it retains only non-empty-string; those are genuine FPs against the length proof.
